answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it may place orders or earn reputation. The ledger links that bond to a unique, scarce resource, and slashes it when an identity is caught coordinating fraud; a delta in behavior can trigger review, but is not proof by itself. Honest agents recover their stake, while an attacker running a grove of disposable accounts must lock up capital for each one and risks losing it, making a haven of cheap fake identities costly to maintain.
